msg: Google API key literal sits in the page source — anyone who opens View Source has it. Restrict the key by HTTP referrer or move the call server-side before you publish.
AWS access key id in client-side HTML. Rotate it and sign requests from a backend — a browser page cannot keep this secret.
Stripe SECRET key (sk_live_) in the page. Only pk_ publishable keys belong in a browser. Roll this key in the Stripe dashboard now.
Slack token in the page source. Revoke it and call Slack from a server, not from the visitor's browser.
A PEM private key block is pasted into this HTML file. Delete it, rotate the key pair, and never ship a private key to a static host.
Firebase-style apiKey literal in inline script. Lock the project with security rules and App Check — a published config without rules is an open database.
A credential is assigned to a literal string in this page. Move it behind a request your server makes, then rotate the value you just exposed.
user:password embedded in a URL. Credentials in a URL leak through history, logs and the Referer header. Remove them before publishing.
A localhost URL works in your preview and dies for every visitor. Point it at the public origin, or make it a relative path.
A private LAN address is hard-coded here. It resolves on your machine only, and it tells strangers your internal network layout.
A file:/// URL only opens from your own disk. Browsers block it from a web page, so this asset will be missing once published.
An absolute path from your own disk is used as src/href. It breaks on the host and it prints your username into the page.
Plain http:// resource on a page that will be served over https. Browsers block or downgrade it — switch the URL to https://.
Form posts over plain http://. Whatever the visitor types travels in clear text. Change the action to https://.
A leftover robots noindex tag. The page will publish fine and then never appear in search — the failure nobody notices for weeks.
Third-party script pinned to @latest. The vendor can change your live page at any moment. Pin an exact version.
A source map reference is shipped with the page, handing readers your unminified source. Drop it from the production build.
A credential is sitting inside an HTML comment. Comments ship to the browser — commenting a secret out does not hide it.
A placeholder or TODO marker survived into the page you are about to publish. Fill it in or delete the block.
Debug console output left in the page. It is noise at best and it prints your data objects to anyone with DevTools open.
A debug flag is still switched on. Set it to false so the published page does not run its development branch.
External script loaded with no integrity hash. If that CDN account is ever taken over, the attacker runs code on your page. Add integrity and crossorigin.
target="_blank" without rel="noopener". The page you link to can reach back into this tab. Add rel="noopener".
The copyright year in this page is older than today. Visitors read a stale year as an abandoned site; generated markup gets this wrong constantly.
